lead_finder.what: Lead Finder, a Python tool that runs on GitHub Actions and finds local businesses through Google Maps.
how: It checks the data is real: the listing is open, the phone number is valid, the website is live and the email domain actually receives mail.
It scores buying intent from customer reviews and public posts, using rules plus an AI check.
It shortlists the strongest leads and emails them.
It has screened more than 13,000 businesses and generated 153 sample pages for outreach.
lead_finder.limit: It has no front end, so nobody else can use it yet.

localsignal.what: LocalSignal, the platform version of Lead Finder.
how: Someone describes what they do and picks the business types, cities and leads per day they want.
It then finds matching local businesses and emails the leads daily.
It has a signup page, a settings dashboard, AI suggestions for which types of business to target, rate limiting and renewal reminders.
localsignal.limit: I built it and I use it myself. It has no outside users yet.

how: It rejects its own scripts when they break a rule and saves each mistake as a lesson the next attempt reads.

facts: My content system's voice read '24x7' as '24 x 7' instead of 'twenty four by seven'.
Looking into it, I found more words and symbols the voice got wrong: prices that ran into the next word, '4K' read as '4 thousand', 'show/hide' turned into nonsense.
I built a pronunciation list, and now every script is checked for words the voice would say wrong before it is recorded.
My content system rejects its own scripts when they break a rule.
Each rejection is saved as a lesson with the exact mistake: what was written, where, and why it failed.
The next attempt reads that lesson, and if a run fails, it starts again by itself.
